title: LLM Summit field notes — creative ops and quick experiments
content:
Quick, messy capture of talks / hallway convos / ideas. Not polished. Use as a seed for a short internal write-up and a two-week spike.

High-level theme I kept hearing: composition + episodic affordances. Not just retrieving text, but stitching small stateful tools to let models act with low-latency local memory. Workshops pushed the idea that cheap, small KV stores + cache-aware routing beats monolithic long-context models for many UXs.

Notes by talk / convo:
- Workshop: "Episodic LLMs for Productive Agents" — main takeaway: store short-lived, recency-weighted traces (2–8 turns) in a tiny LRU-KV near the serving node. Use bloom-ish filters to avoid unnecessary fetches. They reported 30–50% fewer cold retrievals and 10–20ms median latency improvement on local setups.
- Talk: "Compositional Tool Chains" (poster) — argued for micro-tools that can be called deterministically (formatters, ontology normalizers, small QA models) chained by a lightweight planner. Planner should prefer idempotent ops to simplify rollbacks.
- Panel: "RAG economics at scale" — ops teams emphasize: network I/O and small-query overheads dominate when embeddings are cheap. Push: cache embedding vectors for frequent queries and use delta-embeddings for streaming session updates.

Open questions / hypotheses to test quickly:
1) Cache-first routing: if prefix hits in KV cache (top-k tokens or last-turn embedding sim > 0.85), short-circuit to cached context and skip external vector DB fetch. Hypothesis: reduces P95 latency by ~25% for interactive flows.
2) Micro-tool fallback: when model confidence < threshold, call deterministic tool (regex normalizer / small grammar model) instead of expensive larger model. Hypothesis: reduces hallucination surface for structured outputs.
3) Episodic compaction: compress last N turns into a single compact embedding via a learned combiner every M turns to keep cache footprint small. Tradeoff: quality drift vs storage.

Proposed 2-week spike (MVP):
- Objective: validate cache-first routing + micro-tool fallback on a small chat demo (customer support style).
- Tasks:
  * Week 1: instrument baseline using hosted-api with current routing (no cache). Collect latency distribution and top-k retrieval counts on a ~1k-session mocked workload.
  * Week 1: implement tiny in-process KV cache (LRU, store: last-turn tokens + embedding, ttl 30m). Add cache-first path to our local test harness.
  * Week 2: add micro-tool layer (simple JSON schema validator + date normalizer + entity canonicalizer). Integrate with planner: call tool when predicted schema-failure probability > 0.6 (quick logistic classifier trained on a small seed set).
  * Week 2: run A/B for 24h and capture: P50/P95 latency, tokens per session, external vector DB QPS, schema-failure rate, user-simulated acceptance (binary).

Metrics to log (minimum):
- P50/P95 latency (ms) per route (model-only, cache-hit, fallback-tool)
- External vector DB QPS and % requests avoided by cache
- Schema-failure rate (pre / post tool)
- Effective cost delta ($ per 1k sessions) approximate using hosted pricing assumptions

Quick experiment notes (commands / snippets to try locally):
- Generate small seed sessions: python tools/gen_sessions.py --intent customer-refund --n 1000 --noise 0.2
- Simple cache API (pseudo): PUT /cache/session_id -> {embedding:..., tokens:..., ts:...} GET /cache/prefix_match -> best hit if sim>0.85
- Train tiny classifier: train_classifier.py --train data/schema_fail_seeds.json --model small-svm --output model.pkl

Evaluation heuristics I care about (qualitative):
- Does the cached prefix actually contain the determinative info (i.e., avoiding retrieval improves coherence)?
- Are tool outputs terser but more correct? Where do they break (edge cases)?
- How often does compaction lose salient info (false negatives)?

Follow-ups / reminders:
- Talk to Ops: ask for typical vector DB cost numbers at production QPS (ping @Asha).
- Draft short internal doc: "Cache-first routing pattern" — include sample config for routing policy, TTL guidance, and safety notes.
- Pull examples from summit slides: get permission to re-use the planner diagram (confluence link above).

Random ideas overheard (for later):
- Use tiny bloom filters to prefilter candidate keys in vector DB shards to reduce cross-shard fans.
- Store ephemeral user intents as integer-coded features (32-bit) rather than full embed vectors for frequent session reuse.
- Hybrid quantization where we keep the freshest embeddings in float32 and cold ones in 8-bit to get best of latency + storage.

Immediate action items for me:
- Monday: spin up baseline run and collect metrics (ETA: Mon EOD).
- Tuesday: wire in in-process cache and run smoke tests with 200 sessions.
- End of Week: present a 10-min demo + metrics to applied-ml weekly.

Notes-to-self: keep write-up light, include concrete numbers (latency/cost) and at least 2 worked examples showing how cache-first routing changes the call graph.

End of dump.

(If I don't get back to it: move to backlog and share with Asha/Kai to pick up)
